server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (fd34222) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0, 64-bit

config.$comment: Pre-registered design (sized for a short report). Factors, levels and replications are fixed BEFORE any run; the analysis reads this file, so no cell can be quietly dropped.

strategies.naive: Baseline. READ COMMITTED: SELECT status; check in application code; unconditional UPDATE. The 'feral' read-check-write pattern.
strategies.conditional_update: CineBook's design. One UPDATE … WHERE status='AVAILABLE' RETURNING; all-or-nothing by comparing the row count.
strategies.pessimistic_sorted: SELECT … FOR UPDATE on all requested seats in one statement ordered by seat (consistent lock order), then UPDATE.
strategies.pessimistic_unordered: SELECT … FOR UPDATE one seat at a time in the client's request order (inconsistent lock order).
strategies.optimistic_version: Read status+version without locks; UPDATE … WHERE version = read version (Kung & Robinson style validation).
strategies.serializable: The naive read-check-write code, but under SERIALIZABLE isolation (PostgreSQL SSI).
strategies.advisory_lock: Coarse pessimism: pg_advisory_xact_lock(showtime) then naive read-check-write.

E1.title: Hot seat: correctness under contention
E1.question: RQ1 — Does each strategy prevent double booking when c clients request the same seat at the same instant?
E1.workload: single seat, every client requests it

E2.title: Overlapping multi-seat requests: deadlocks, aborts and correctness
E2.question: RQ3 — How do strategies behave when clients request several seats from a small pool in random order?
E2.workload: pool of 10 seats; each client requests 3 random seats in random order

E3.title: Low contention: latency and throughput cost
E3.question: RQ2 — What latency/throughput does each correct strategy cost when clients do NOT collide?
E3.workload: each client books its own distinct seats, 5 sequential holds per client per trial

E5.title: Platform generalisation: embedded PGlite vs networked Postgres
E5.question: RQ5 — Does the test platform change the conclusion? (validity threat for local testing)

E4a.title: Live read latency vs PRD target (p95 < 200 ms)

E4b.title: Live hot-seat race through the deployed API
